## Question 1: Inference about a Population Mean (13 marks)

Each multiple-choice question is worth 1 mark.

### Part A: Oyster Shell Height at a New Lease Site

An oyster grower in Prince Edward Island knows that market oysters from the original lease have a population mean shell height of $80$ mm. The grower opens a new lease site and selects a random sample of $25$ market-size oysters from the several thousand oysters there. The sample has mean shell height $\bar{x}=81.9$ mm and sample standard deviation $s=5.0$ mm. A dotplot of the sample is approximately symmetric and shows no outliers.

Before collecting the data, the grower planned to test whether the population mean shell height at the new site is **greater than** $80$ mm. Use $\alpha=0.05$. You may use
$$t=\frac{\bar{x}-\mu_0}{s/\sqrt{n}}$$

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\arabic*.},leftmargin=1.8em]

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Which of the following best describes the population parameter $\mu$?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item The historical mean shell height, $80$ mm, at the original lease
  \item The proportion of oysters at the new site that are taller than $80$ mm
  \item The population mean shell height of all market-size oysters at the new lease site
  \item The mean shell height, $81.9$ mm, of the $25$ sampled oysters
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Which pair of hypotheses matches the grower's question?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $H_0:\mu=80$ \quad versus \quad $H_a:\mu>80$
  \item $H_0:\mu=81.9$ \quad versus \quad $H_a:\mu>81.9$
  \item $H_0:\bar{x}=80$ \quad versus \quad $H_a:\bar{x}>80$
  \item $H_0:\mu=80$ \quad versus \quad $H_a:\mu\neq80$
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
What is the estimated standard error of $\bar{x}$?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $5.000$ mm
  \item $1.021$ mm
  \item $0.200$ mm
  \item $1.000$ mm
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
What are the test statistic and its degrees of freedom?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $t=-1.900$ with $df=24$
  \item $t=1.900$ with $df=24$
  \item $t=1.900$ with $df=25$
  \item $t=0.380$ with $df=24$
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\newpage

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Using the $t$-distribution table, which range contains the P-value for the grower's test?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $0.010<P\text{-value}<0.025$
  \item $P\text{-value}>0.100$
  \item $0.025<P\text{-value}<0.050$
  \item $0.050<P\text{-value}<0.100$
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Which statement gives the correct decision and conclusion at $\alpha=0.05$?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item Reject $H_0$. This proves that the population mean shell height at the new site is exactly $81.9$ mm.
  \item Reject $H_0$. The data give statistically significant evidence that the sample mean shell height is greater than $80$ mm.
  \item Fail to reject $H_0$, because the P-value is greater than $0.05$.
  \item Reject $H_0$. The data give statistically significant evidence that the population mean shell height at the new site is greater than $80$ mm.
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Suppose the grower had instead planned to test whether the population mean shell height at the new site \textbf{differs from} $80$ mm, using the same data. Which statement is correct?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $0.050<P\text{-value}<0.100$, so fail to reject $H_0$
  \item The P-value is the same as in the one-sided test, so reject $H_0$
  \item $0.0125<P\text{-value}<0.025$, so reject $H_0$
  \item $0.025<P\text{-value}<0.050$, so reject $H_0$
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\end{enumerate}

### Part B: Resting Heart Rate of Racehorses

A harness-racing trainer in Prince Edward Island wants to know whether an $8$-week conditioning program **lowers** the mean resting heart rate of standardbred racehorses. The trainer measures the resting heart rate (beats per minute) of the same $15$ horses before and after the program and defines each difference as
$$d=\text{after}-\text{before}$$
The $15$ differences have mean $\bar{d}=-4.0$ beats per minute and standard deviation $s_d=5.0$ beats per minute. A dotplot of the differences is roughly symmetric with no outliers. Use $\alpha=0.05$.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\arabic*.},leftmargin=1.8em,start=8]

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Which description of the analysis is correct?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item One sample of $15$ differences, analyzed with $df=15$
  \item One sample of $15$ differences, analyzed with $df=14$
  \item Two independent samples of $15$ horses each, analyzed with $df=28$
  \item One sample of $30$ heart-rate measurements, analyzed with $df=29$
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Which pair of hypotheses matches the trainer's question?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $H_0:\mu_d=0$ \quad versus \quad $H_a:\mu_d\neq0$
  \item $H_0:\bar{d}=0$ \quad versus \quad $H_a:\bar{d}<0$
  \item $H_0:\mu_d=0$ \quad versus \quad $H_a:\mu_d>0$
  \item $H_0:\mu_d=0$ \quad versus \quad $H_a:\mu_d<0$
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
What are the standard error of $\bar{d}$ and the test statistic?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $SE=1.291$ and $t=-3.098$
  \item $SE=5.000$ and $t=-0.800$
  \item $SE=0.333$ and $t=-12.000$
  \item $SE=1.291$ and $t=3.098$
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Using the $t$-distribution table, which range contains the P-value for the trainer's test?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $P\text{-value}<0.0005$
  \item $0.005<P\text{-value}<0.010$
  \item $0.0025<P\text{-value}<0.005$
  \item $0.010<P\text{-value}<0.025$
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Using $t^*=2.145$, what is the $95\%$ confidence interval for $\mu_d$?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $(1.231,\ 6.769)$ beats per minute
  \item $(-6.769,\ -1.231)$ beats per minute
  \item $(-14.725,\ 6.725)$ beats per minute
  \item $(-6.530,\ -1.470)$ beats per minute
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Suppose the trainer had instead defined $d=\text{before}-\text{after}$. Which statement is correct?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $\bar{d}=4.0$, $t=3.098$, $H_a:\mu_d>0$, and the conclusion reverses
  \item $\bar{d}=-4.0$, $t=-3.098$, $H_a:\mu_d>0$, and the P-value and conclusion are unchanged
  \item $\bar{d}=4.0$, $t=3.098$, $H_a:\mu_d<0$, and the P-value and conclusion are unchanged
  \item $\bar{d}=4.0$, $t=3.098$, $H_a:\mu_d>0$, and the P-value and conclusion are unchanged
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\end{enumerate}

## Question 2: Nitrate in PEI Private Wells (7 marks)

Each multiple-choice question is worth 1 mark.

A provincial report from previous years estimated that $10\%$ of private wells in Prince Edward Island had nitrate levels above the drinking-water guideline. This year, a provincial agency tests a random sample of $900$ private wells from the tens of thousands of private wells in the province. Of these, $117$ wells have nitrate levels above the guideline.

The agency wants to determine whether the proportion of private wells above the guideline has changed from $10\%$. Use $\alpha=0.05$. You may use
$$z=\frac{\hat{p}-p_0}{\sqrt{p_0(1-p_0)/n}}\qquad\qquad \hat{p}\pm z^*\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})}{n}}$$

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\arabic*.},leftmargin=1.8em]

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Which of the following best describes the population parameter $p$?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item The proportion of all private wells in PEI with nitrate levels above the guideline this year
  \item The sample proportion, $0.13$, of the $900$ tested wells above the guideline
  \item The number of tested wells, $117$, above the guideline
  \item The proportion, $0.10$, reported in previous years
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Which pair of hypotheses matches the agency's question?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $H_0:p=0.10$ \quad versus \quad $H_a:p>0.10$
  \item $H_0:p=0.13$ \quad versus \quad $H_a:p\neq0.13$
  \item $H_0:p=0.10$ \quad versus \quad $H_a:p\neq0.10$
  \item $H_0:\hat{p}=0.10$ \quad versus \quad $H_a:\hat{p}\neq0.10$
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Which statement correctly checks the large-count condition for the \textbf{test}?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $n=900\ge30$, so the condition is met
  \item $np_0=90\ge10$ and $n(1-p_0)=810\ge10$, so the condition is met
  \item $np_0=90$ is less than $X=117$, so the condition is not met
  \item $X=117\ge15$ and $n-X=783\ge15$, so the condition is met
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
What are the sample proportion, the null standard error and the test statistic?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $\hat{p}=0.130$, \ $SE_0=0.0112$, \ $z=2.676$
  \item $\hat{p}=0.100$, \ $SE_0=0.0112$, \ $z=2.676$
  \item $\hat{p}=0.130$, \ $SE_0=0.010$, \ $z=-3.000$
  \item $\hat{p}=0.130$, \ $SE_0=0.010$, \ $z=3.000$
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\newpage

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Using the $df=\infty$ row of the table, which statement gives the correct P-value range and decision?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $0.002<P\text{-value}<0.005$, so reject $H_0$
  \item $0.002<P\text{-value}<0.005$, so fail to reject $H_0$
  \item $0.020<P\text{-value}<0.050$, so reject $H_0$
  \item $0.001<P\text{-value}<0.0025$, so reject $H_0$
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Using $z^*=1.960$, what is the $95\%$ large-sample confidence interval for $p$?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item $(0.110,\ 0.150)$
  \item $(0.078,\ 0.122)$
  \item $(0.108,\ 0.152)$
  \item $(0.112,\ 0.148)$
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\item \begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
Which statement correctly interprets the confidence interval and relates it to the test?
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\Alph*.},itemsep=0.15em]
  \item The interval contains the sample proportion $0.13$, so we fail to reject $H_0$.
  \item We are $95\%$ confident that the proportion of all PEI private wells above the guideline is in the interval. The interval excludes $0.10$, which is consistent with rejecting $H_0$.
  \item There is a $95\%$ probability that $p$ lies in the interval, so $H_0$ is rejected.
  \item About $95\%$ of private wells have nitrate levels within the interval.
\end{enumerate}
\end{minipage}

\end{enumerate}
